nodes.name: P-Co/Co(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Sodium hypophosphite-induced electrodeposition strategy was used to construct phosphorus-doped cobalt and cobalt hydroxide (P-Co/Co(OH)₂) composites. Optimal electrodeposition time of 900 s and dosage of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O of 2.0 g were determined. The sample exhibits heterointerfaces of metallic cobalt and Co(OH)₂ on its surface.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: one-step electrodeposition process with optimal electrodeposition time of 900 s and dosage of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O of 2.0 g

nodes.source_text: a sodium hypophosphite-induced electrodeposition strategy was proposed to construct phosphorus-doped cobalt and cobalt hydroxide (P-Co/Co(OH)₂) composites... optimal electrodeposition time and dosage of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O were determined to be 900 s and 2.0 g, respectively

nodes.name: Co@Co(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The Co@Co(OH)₂ microsphere with core-shell structure (metallic cobalt core, Co(OH)₂ shell) was obtained by one-step electrodeposition process without phosphorus source/addition of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O into the electrolyte.

The electrocatalytic HER performance of P - Co / Co(OH)_2 and Co@Co(OH)_2 was evaluated in alkaline condition (1 M KOH) using the three-electrode configuration... P - Co / Co(OH)_2 only required a low overpotential of 36.7 mV to drive a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} ... It can homogeneously sustain a current density of about 250 mA cm^{-2} for 55 h ... The Faradic efficiency was determined to be about 98%
Co@Co(OH)_2 exhibits a larger overpotential of 217.6 mV ... retaining only 59.1% of its initial current density after 55 h. The Tafel slopes of Co@Co(OH)_2 were determined to be 73.9 mV dec^{-1}

nodes.characterization_summary: All diffraction peaks of both catalysts attribute to hexagonal cobalt (JCPDS 05-0727); (002) plane of P-Co/Co(OH)₂ shows left shift due to phosphorus incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S1A (Supporting Information), all of the diffraction peaks of both samples attribute to hexagonal cobalt (JCPDS card No. 05-0727). Notably, the (002) plane of P-Co/Co(OH)₂ exhibited a left shift as compared to Co@Co(OH)₂...

nodes.characterization_summary: Amorphous Co(OH)₂ phase confirmed by peaks at ≈470 and 510 cm⁻¹ corresponding to Co-O vibrations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous phase of Co(OH)₂ was confirmed by Raman measurements. Two peaks at ≈470 and 510 cm⁻¹ correspond to Co-O vibrations (Figure S1B, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Both catalysts consist of aggregated spheres; P-Co/Co(OH)₂ shows flocculent surface while Co@Co(OH)₂ shows hierarchical surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FESEM images demonstrated that both samples consisted of aggregated spheres (Figure S2A,C, Supporting Information). ... The P-Co/Co(OH)₂ exhibited a flocculent surface... in sharp contrast to the hierarchical surface observed for the Co@Co(OH)₂...

nodes.characterization_summary: P-Co/Co(OH)₂ exposes heterointerfaces of metallic cobalt and amorphous Co(OH)₂; Co@Co(OH)₂ shows hierarchical structure with only amorphous Co(OH)₂ exposed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images further confirmed the flocculent surface of P-Co/Co(OH)₂ and the hierarchical structure of Co@Co(OH)₂ (Figure 1B,F).

nodes.characterization_summary: P-Co/Co(OH)₂ shows lattice fringe of 0.21 nm for Co (002) plane with expanded fringe from P incorporation; Co@Co(OH)₂ shows 0.22 nm for Co (100) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringe of 0.21 nm in the HRTEM image corresponds to the Co (002) plane (Figure 1D). ... The lattice fringe in the crystalline part was determined to be 0.22 nm, belonging to the Co (100) plane (Figure 1H).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns for both catalysts consistent with hexagonal cobalt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns for both samples were consistent with the hexagonal cobalt (Figure 1E,I).

nodes.characterization_summary: P-Co/Co(OH)₂ shows uniform Co (95.66 at%), O (2.13 at%), P (2.21 at%); Co@Co(OH)₂ shows Co (94.49 at%), O (5.51 at%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As can be seen in Figures S3 and S4 (Supporting Information), uniform dispersion of Co (95.66%), O (2.13%), and P (2.21%) elements was observed in P-Co/Co(OH)₂ microspheres, while only Co (94.49%) and O (5.51%) elements were detected in Co@Co(OH)₂ microspheres.

nodes.characterization_summary: P-Co/Co(OH)₂ XPS survey shows Co 24.96%, O 63.72%, P 11.32%; P 2p peaks at 129.3, 130.7 eV (M-P), 132.9 eV (P-ox); Co 2p oxidized Co at 781.2/796.9 eV (ΔE=15.7 eV), metallic Co at 777.9 eV only in P-Co/Co(OH)₂; O 1s at 533.4 eV (H₂O), 531.4 eV (M-OH), 529.2 eV (M-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: These findings further supported by XPS survey results, with Co of 24.96%, O of 63.72%, and P of 11.32% (Figure S6, Supporting Information). The P 2p spectrum exhibited three main peaks at the position of 129.3, 130.7, and 132.9 eV (Figure 2A).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows metallic Co presence and low oxidation state Co; EXAFS shows Co-Co, Co-O bonds in both catalysts and Co-P in P-Co/Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray adsorption near edge spectra (XANES) of both samples and cobalt foil at Co-edge region exhibit analogous adsorption edges, suggesting the presence of metallic cobalt... The extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra display the Co-O, Co-Co bonds in Co(OH)₂ and the Co-Co bond in metallic cobalt for both samples (Figure 2E).

nodes.characterization_summary: P-Co/Co(OH)₂ contact angle 46° indicating better hydrophilicity than Co@Co(OH)₂ at 106°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S16 (Supporting Information) shows that the average contact angle of P-Co/Co(OH)₂ is 46°, significantly smaller than that of Co/Co(OH)₂ (106°).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR shows OH_ad peak at 3730 cm⁻¹ intensity stable over time for P-Co/Co(OH)₂ but increasing for Co@Co(OH)₂, indicating weaker hydroxyl adsorption on P-Co/Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) analyses provide direct evidence distinct behavior of hydroxyl species on the both samples (Figure 5B,C).
